The oak tree in the backyard of 42 Maple Street had been a target for lightning strikes, hailstorms, and the occasional rogue baseball, but it had never faced the combined engineering ambition of Leo and Sam.
It started on the first day of June with a single, ambitious sketch on the back of a grocery receipt. Leo, who had just finished reading a book on structural integrity, drew a spiral staircase. Sam, who had just finished watching a documentary on medieval fortifications, drew a drawbridge.
"We can’t do both," Leo said, tapping his pencil against the table.
"Why not?" Sam countered. "We have three months."
They had exactly twelve weeks.
The first week was a disaster. They tried to build the platform using only the tools in Leo’s father’s garage. The drill bit snapped. The hammer slipped. The first plank they nailed to the trunk split down the middle. They sat on the grass, sweating and frustrated, eating warm popsicles.
"Maybe we should just buy a kit," Leo suggested, his voice small.
"No," Sam said, wiping sweat from his forehead. "We build it. We just need better tools."
